literature_note: SELENOW has direct NAFLD-specific experimental evidence and human-liver transcriptomic support. The 2024 study links SelW to metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial ROS, pyroptosis and macrophage cGAS-STING signaling. This provides unusually direct biological context for a high-ranked CpG, although no methylation-to-expression link for cg07953015 has been demonstrated.
selection_reason: Selected because it combines statistical rank 3, strict-subset membership, direct gene annotation and direct NAFLD-specific experimental/human-liver evidence.

human_masld_evidence: Adjacent-gene context only — WWTR1/TAZ is markedly increased in hepatocytes in human NASH compared with normal/steatotic liver.
human_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Adjacent-gene context only — human NASH liver showed TAZ elevation; fibrosis causality is supported primarily by experimental models.
experimental_masld_evidence: Yes for adjacent WWTR1 — hepatocyte TAZ silencing prevented/reversed NASH inflammation and fibrosis, whereas TAZ expression promoted NASH features in mice.
experimental_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Yes for adjacent WWTR1 — multiple NASH models, including hepatocyte-humanized mice, support a causal profibrotic TAZ pathway.
hepatic_metabolism_evidence: Yes for adjacent WWTR1 — mechanistically links hepatocyte stress to IHH-dependent hepatic stellate-cell activation.
evidence_directness: Intergenic enhancer 394 bp from the WWTR1 TSS. The disease evidence is exceptionally strong for WWTR1, but no direct evidence links cg08928408 methylation to WWTR1 expression or function.
literature_note: WWTR1/TAZ is one of the strongest MASLD/MASH-fibrosis genes near any intergenic Top-30 locus. Because cg08928408 lies only 394 bp from its TSS and is enhancer-annotated, the neighborhood is biologically notable; nevertheless, the CpG must be described as 'near WWTR1', not as a WWTR1 regulatory CpG.
selection_reason: Selected because of statistical rank 5 and unusually close proximity to a gene with strong human and causal MASH-fibrosis evidence, while explicitly preserving the unresolved CpG-to-gene link.

human_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Adjacent-gene context only — EMP1 is reported in human fibrotic liver/HSC signatures.
experimental_masld_evidence: Adjacent-gene context only — EMP1 has mechanistic MASLD-IRI/HSC evidence, but this is not evidence for cg24680129.

selection_reason: Not selected despite statistical rank 6 because the appealing biology belongs to a relatively distant nearest gene and the CpG-to-EMP1 link is unvalidated.

human_masld_evidence: No direct MASLD-specific ARHGEF12 study identified.

evidence_directness: Direct gene-body annotation to ARHGEF12. Evidence is gene/pathway-level and does not establish a functional consequence of cg05099464 methylation.
literature_note: ARHGEF12 (LARG) participates in Wnt/Gli1-dependent RhoA activation in hepatic stellate cells and cirrhotic portal hypertension, with supporting human liver and mouse/HSC experiments. The evidence is liver-fibrosis-specific but not MASLD-specific.
selection_reason: Selected because it is statistical rank 7, directly gene-annotated, and has mechanistic and human-liver support for a relevant hepatic stellate-cell/fibrosis pathway.

experimental_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Yes — SphK2 depletion increased fibrosis in a diet-induced MASH model.

literature_note: SPHK2 has direct human MASLD/MASH liver evidence and multiple mechanistic studies linking it to triglyceride handling, VLDL secretion, redox balance, inflammation and fibrosis. Across studies, gene function appears protective in several genetic models, although sphingolipid-pathway effects can be context dependent.
selection_reason: Selected because it combines direct gene annotation, strong statistical support and unusually broad, direct human and experimental MASLD/MASH evidence.

experimental_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Yes — GPX4 isoform manipulation affected steatohepatitis/fibrosis in mouse MAFLD models; ferroptosis biology is cell- and isoform-dependent.
hepatic_metabolism_evidence: Yes — central regulator of glutathione-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification and ferroptosis.

literature_note: GPX4 remains one of the most biologically interpretable candidates because it directly connects the methylation signal to ferroptosis and lipid-peroxidation biology in human and experimental MASLD. Mechanistic direction should be described carefully because canonical and inducible GPX4 isoforms, and different liver cell types, can have different effects.
selection_reason: Selected because of direct gene annotation and strong human plus experimental MASLD evidence for GPX4/ferroptosis, despite statistical rank 16 and moderate heterogeneity across contrasts.

human_masld_evidence: No dedicated human MASLD DDR2 validation identified in the reviewed primary studies.
human_liver_fibrosis_evidence: No direct human fibrosis cohort used as primary evidence here.
experimental_masld_evidence: Yes — HFD/db/db and primary-hepatocyte experiments show DDR2 suppresses steatosis/lipogenesis through AMPK/ACC signaling.
experimental_liver_fibrosis_evidence: Yes — chronic CCl4 experiments demonstrate a direct DDR2 role in hepatic fibrosis/HSC-macrophage interactions; effects are context-dependent across injury settings.

evidence_directness: Direct DDR2 gene-body annotation. Gene-level liver evidence is strong, but cg24249925 has not been shown to regulate DDR2.
literature_note: DDR2 bridges metabolic and fibrotic liver biology. Recent MASLD experiments indicate a protective role against hepatocyte lipogenesis, while chronic-injury work shows DDR2 can attenuate fibrosis through HSC/macrophage interactions. The fibrosis literature is context-dependent, so simple directional claims should be avoided.
selection_reason: Selected because of direct gene annotation, strict-subset membership and experimental evidence spanning hepatic steatosis and fibrosis.

literature_note: LONRF1 has direct NASH-liver single-cell context, particularly in LSECs and Kupffer cells, but current evidence is descriptive rather than mechanistic. This makes it disease-specific but substantially weaker than causal evidence for SELENOW, SPHK2, GPX4 or DDR2.
selection_reason: Selected because it is directly annotated and has NASH-specific liver single-cell evidence, adding a non-parenchymal-cell/tissue-remodeling angle despite lower statistical rank and limited mechanistic validation.
